recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中箭頭指出兩顆組織球，細胞質豐富、淡藍綠色細顆粒狀，其中一顆邊緣可見一小顆紅棕色的被吞噬物；背景為大量深染圓核的晚期紅血球母細胞，呈紅系增生，符合溶血性貧血的反應性組織球。
features: Large histiocytes (arrows) with abundant, pale blue-green, finely granular cytoplasm and a single oval nucleus
One histiocyte (right arrow) has a small reddish-brown inclusion at its edge, possibly an ingested red cell fragment or pigment
Left histiocyte shows a smeared, poorly delineated cytoplasm with a few darker blue granules
Background erythroid hyperplasia with numerous small round dense-nucleated normoblasts
Occasional granulocytic precursors and a basophilic/mast-type granulated cell at the upper right; dark stain precipitate present
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular specimen with marked erythroid hyperplasia composed predominantly of late normoblasts. Two large histiocytes (arrows) are present with abundant pale blue-green, finely granular cytoplasm and oval nuclei; one contains a small reddish-brown peripheral inclusion that may represent ingested red cell material or pigment, although resolution limits interpretation. Scattered granulocytic precursors and stain precipitate are also seen. Findings are consistent with reactive histiocytes in the setting of increased red cell destruction, as in hemolytic anemia.

ddx.vs: HLH shows multiple histiocytes with clearly engulfed intact erythrocytes, platelets, or nucleated cells together with clinical criteria, rather than a single equivocal inclusion.
Primary storage disorders show sheets of sea-blue or foamy histiocytes and require enzymatic or genetic confirmation.
Hemosiderin appears as coarse dark blue-black or golden-brown granules and is confirmed by Prussian blue staining.
CDA shows binucleated or multinucleated erythroblasts and internuclear bridging, which are not evident in this field.
